      PUBLIC INPUT
        1. Two 15-minute Public Input sessions will be allowed during each Council
           Meeting. Time will be divided equally among those wishing to speak, however,
           no person will be allowed to speak for more than 5 minutes.
        2. No person may address the council more than twice on any issue in any
           meeting. Comments must be addressed to the Chair and must not be personal
           or derogatory about any other person.
        3. Any questions must be directly related to the topic being discussed and must
           be addressed to the Chair only, who after consultation with Council and Town
           Administrator, will determine if the question can be answered at that time.
           Questions cannot be directed to an individual Councilor and must not be
           personal in nature. Issues raised during Public Input, which cannot be resolved
           or answered at that time, or which require additional discussion or research,
           will be noted by the Town Administrator who will be responsible for researching
           and responding to the comment directly during normal work hours or by
           bringing to the Council for discussion at a subsequent meeting. The Chair
           reserves the right to end questioning if the questions depart from clarification to
           deliberation.
        4. Council members may request a comment be added to New Business at a
           subsequent meeting.
        5. No one may speak during Public Input except the person acknowledged by the
           Chair. Direct questions or comments from the audience are not permitted
           during Public Input.

Town Council
STAFF REPORT

To:            Town Council
Title:         Second Public Hearing for the Amendment to Ordinance #00-26 (Signage
               Regulations for Town Roads) and Adoption of Ordinance #26-01 (No Through
               Trucking)
Meeting:       Town Council - 13 May 2026
Department:    Administration
Staff Contact: Leann McLaughlin, Project Coordinator

BACKGROUND INFORMATION:
The Highway Safety Advisory Board reviewed the existing No Through Trucking provisions and
identified that the current language, contained as a brief section within the Signage Regulations for
Town Roads Ordinance, is insufficient for effective enforcement by the Police Department. In
response, the Board developed a standalone No Through Trucking Ordinance to provide clearer
authority and enforceability. The proposed ordinance has been reviewed by both the Police
Department and the Public Works Department. This action would also amend the Signage
Regulations for Town Roads Ordinance to reference the new ordinance.

Based on comments from the Chair of the Planning Board during the last public hearing, Schedule A
title was revised to say "No Through Trucking Sign Locations" and added a Schedule B titled "No
Through Trucking Roads."

Additional comments received from the Planning Board at their May 4 meeting are as follows:
1. An emergency/detour clause should be added to "Section 4 -- Exemptions"
2. Attention should be given to the Laurel Road/Spruce Court/Evelyn Street neighborhood as
members have commented that this neighborhood is increasingly being used as a cut-through.

RECOMMENDATION:
Open the public hearing.
Discuss.
Listen to any public input.
Review the Planning Board comments provided in the Background Section and determine if Council
would like to move forward with either recommendations.
Close the public hearing.

TOWN ADMINISTRATOR'S RECOMMENDATION:
Conduct public hearing

ATTACHMENTS:
Signage Regulation of Town Roads #00-26 (Red Lined)
Town of Hooksett - 2nd Public Hearing Legal Notice

                       SIGNAGE REGULATION OF TOWN ROADS
                               ORDINANCE # 00-26

The Town of Hooksett ordains that, pursuant to RSA 41:11 of the New Hampshire State Statues
and Section 3.6 of the Hooksett Town Charter, the following ordinance is hereby enacted in the
Town of Hooksett:

SECTION 1

NO PARKING - Parking is prohibited at designated areas as indicated by posted signs. An
inventory list of all approved "No Parking" signs is maintained at the Town Clerk's office and at
the Highway Department for public inspection.

SECTION 1.1

PARKING PROHIBITIONS –
      A. A person shall not park a vehicle upon any street, highway, or town parking facility
         for the principal purpose of displaying it for sale, washing, maintenance or repairs;
         repairs of an emergency nature will be excluded.
      B. A person shall not park a commercial vehicle (as defined below) upon any
         residential street, or town parking facility at any time, unless the actual loading or
         unloading of materials is occurring thereof.
      C. A person in violation of this provision shall be subject to fines and penalties as set
         forth in Administrative Enforcement of Parking Violations Ordinance #00-28, under
         “NO PARKING ZONE”. Violators can be removed under the direction of the
         Hooksett Police Department. Charges for towing and storage shall be paid by the
         owner for release of the vehicle.

Commercial Vehicle: A motor vehicle or trailer, not including a resident’s personal vehicle that
has been modified to accommodate a disability, or a vehicle used exclusively for agriculture or
farming when located on and accessory to a permitted agricultural use, that exhibits one or
more of the following characteristics:
       1. Has more than two (2) axles.
       2. Has a height greater than seven (7) feet.
       3. Has a length greater than (19) feet.
       4. Has a Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) of greater than ten thousand (10,000)
           pounds.
       5. Is registered as other than “passenger”, “antique” or “street rod” vehicle, and is
           designed, maintained, or used primarily for the transportation of passengers,
           property or freight for hire, compensation, or profit.
       6. Has special ramps, hoists, buckets, cranes, arms, platforms, or similar features
           designed primarily to lift, tow or carry motor vehicles, equipment, trailers, materials or
           workers.

SECTION 2

NO THROUGH TRUCKING - Trucks exceeding three ton GVW are prohibited on roads with
signage marked "No Through Trucking". Exclusions shall be trucks making a delivery to a
home or business on the prohibited road. An inventory list of all approved "No Through
Trucks" signs and designated "No Through Truck" streets are maintained at the Town Clerk's
office and at the Highway Department for public inspection.See No Through Trucking
Ordinance #26-01 for additional information. An inventory list of all approved “No Through
Trucks” signs and designated “No Though Trucking” streets are attached to the ordinance and
maintained at the Town Clerk’s office and at the Highway Department for public inspection.


                                                 65


                                                                                                        Page 6 of 128
                                                                                            Agenda Item #6.1.


SECTION 3

STOP SIGNS - All stop signs approved by the Town Council shall be posted by the Hooksett
Highway Department and deemed legal and enforceable. An inventory list of all legal stop signs
is maintained at the Town Clerk's office and at the Highway Department for public inspection.

SECTION 4

All other regulatory and advisory signs approved by the Town Council are authorized to be
posted by the Highway Department and deemed legal and enforceable.

SECTION 5

PENALTY - Any person, persons, firm, partnership or corporation, found violating any provision
of this ordinance, shall be fined no more than $1,000.00 for each day such violation continues.

SECTION 6

This ordinance shall become effective upon passage.

ADOPTED: 12/14/94
AMENDED: 1/18/23

                                 NO THROUGH TRUCKING
                                    ORDINANCE #26-01

SECTION 1: PURPOSE AND AUTHORITY
The Town of Hooksett ordains that this ordinance is adopted to protect public safety, preserve
roadway infrastructure, reduce noise and vibration impacts to residential neighborhoods, and
maintain the character of local streets by restricting through-truck traffic on designated
roadways.

This ordinance is enacted pursuant to the Town’s police powers and applicable state law
authorizing municipalities to regulate traffic on local ways.

SECTION 2: DEFINITIONS
No Through Trucking:
The use of a roadway by a truck for the purpose of traveling between two points without an
origin or destination on that roadway. Trucks are prohibited from using the roadway as a
shortcut. Trucks are permitted only when they originate, terminate, or must travel on the
roadway to access:
    • A residence
    • A business
    • A construction site
    • A delivery or service location


Truck:
Any vehicle registered or operated as a commercial motor vehicle, including trucks, truck-
tractors, tractor-trailers, combination vehicles, and vehicles bearing a U.S. Department of
Transportation (DOT) number. This definition excludes passenger vehicles.

Local Delivery or Service:
Travel by a truck for the sole purpose of making a delivery to, pickup from, or providing services
at a residence, business, construction site, or other lawful destination located on a roadway
designated as “No Through Trucking.”

SECTION 3: PROHIBITION
  A. No truck operator shall operate a truck on any roadway posted with official “No Through
      Trucking” signage for the purpose of through travel.
  B. Through travel shall mean travel where the truck’s origin and destination are not located
  on, and do not require access from, the posted roadway.

SECTION 4: EXEMPTIONS


                                                                                                     Page 9 of 128
                                                                                              Agenda Item #6.1.


The following vehicles and activities are exempt from this ordinance:
   1. Trucks making a local delivery, pickup, or service call to a residence, business, or
       construction site located on the posted roadway.
   2. Emergency and public safety vehicles while engaged in official duties.
   3. Town, State, or utility vehicles performing construction, maintenance, repair, or
       emergency response.
   4. School buses and municipal transit vehicles.
   5. Vehicles operating pursuant to a temporary written permit issued by the Highway
       Department or Town Administrator for extraordinary circumstances.

SECTION 5: SIGNAGE AND DESIGNATED ROADWAYS
A. Enforcement of this ordinance shall apply only to roadways that are clearly posted with
Town-approved “No Through Trucking” signage.
B. An inventory list of all approved “No Through Trucking” signs and all designated “No
Through Trucking” roadways shall be maintained at:
   • The Town Clerk’s Office;
   • The Highway Department; and
   • As attached to this Ordinance.
Such records shall be available for public inspection during normal business hours.

SECTION 6: ENFORCEMENT
A. This ordinance shall be enforced by the Hooksett Police Department.
B. Enforcement shall be based on the determination of whether a truck is engaged in prohibited
through travel or permitted local access, as defined herein.

SECTION 7: BURDEN OF PROOF FOR EXEMPTIONS
The operator of a truck claiming an exemption under this ordinance shall, upon request by a law
enforcement officer, provide reasonable documentation or explanation demonstrating eligibility
for the exemption, including proof of a local delivery or service call.

SECTION 8: PENALTIES
  A. Pursuant to RSA 265:9, failure to follow the posted traffic control device (No Through
     Trucking) may be cited and subject to enforcement action.
  B. Each occurrence and each day a violation continues shall constitute a separate offense.

SECTION 9: APPEALS
Any person cited under this ordinance may appeal the citation in accordance with applicable
state law governing traffic.

SECTION 10: SEVERABILITY


                                                                                                  Page 10 of 128
                                                                                                  Agenda Item #6.1.


If any section, subsection, sentence, clause, or phrase of this ordinance is held invalid, such
decision shall not affect the validity of the remaining portions of the ordinance.

SECTION 11: EFFECTIVE DATE
This ordinance shall take effect upon adoption by the Town Council and posting as required by
law.

Town Council
STAFF REPORT

To:            Town Council
Title:         Second Public Hearing for Adoption of New Ordinance #2026-02 Sale of Tax
               Deeded Property "as justice may require"
Meeting:       Town Council - 13 May 2026
Department:    Administration
Staff Contact: André Garron, Town Administrator

BACKGROUND INFORMATION:
RSA 80:80, III governs how a municipality handles tax liens and tax deeded property. RSA 80:80
contains a provision that allows the governing body to authorize the disposal of tax liens or tax
deeded property in alternative ways beyond public auction or sealed bid -- "as justice may require."
The phrase "as justice may require" is a provision that gives the Town Council discretion to dispose of
tax liens or tax deeded property in ways other than public auction or sealed bid, when circumstances
justify it.

Specifically, the section of RSA 80:80, III, states, "III. The governing body may, by a specific article in
the town warrant, or by ordinance, be authorized to dispose of liens or tax deeded properties in a
manner other than as provided in this section, as justice may require. Before proceeding under this
provision, the governing body shall make an affirmative finding that disposal by a method other than
sealed bid or public auction is in the public interest." If the Town Council adopts this section of RSA
80:80, III, "as justice may require" allows a range of options designed to serve fairness and municipal
needs such as engaging a real estate agent to market and sell the property, sell undeveloped parcels
to adjoining landowners to support consolidation for affordable housing, open space or negotiate a
conveyance back to a former owner. It can also address redevelopment, preserve community
character, resolve title complexities or support affordable housing.

Adopting RSA 80:80, III would also provide clarity and reinforce the Town's authority with respect to
prior and future tax-deeded property sales.

RECOMMENDATION:
Open public hearing.
Discuss and take public comment.
Close public hearing.

TOWN ADMINISTRATOR'S RECOMMENDATION:
2nd Public Hearing, Town Council would be able to take action on this item at its May 27 meeting.

           SALE OF TAX DEEDED PROPERTY AS JUSTICE MAY REQUIRE
                            ORDINANCE #26-02


SECTION 1 – PURPOSE AND INTENT
The purpose and intent of this ordinance is to authorize the Town Council to sell tax deeded
property by means other than through public auction or sealed bid, as justice may require.


SECTION 2 – AUTHORIZATION
This ordinance is adopted pursuant to the authority set forth in RSA 80:80, III.


SECTION 3 – REQUIREMENTS
The Town is entitled to sell a tax deeded property “as justice may require”, and thus in a manner
not involving public auction or sealed bid, so long as the Town Council finds that it is in the
public’s interest to do so.


SECTION 4 - DEFINITIONS
For purposes of this ordinance, and consistent with RSA 80:80, VI, the term “as justice may
requires” means that the Town Council, after making an affirmative finding that sale of the
property other than by public auction or sealed bid is in the public interest, may sell a property in
one of the following ways:

   A. Engage a real estate agent or broker to list and sell the property, including a sale
      conditional on the buyer's obtaining development approvals;

   B. Sell undeveloped parcels to abutters for consolidation into adjoining lots for the purpose
      of affordable housing development, preserving open space, or reducing development
      density; or

   C. Convey the property to a former owner, or to a third party for benefit of a former owner,
      upon such reasonable terms as may be agreed to in writing, including the authority of the
      municipality to retain a mortgage interest in the property, or to reimpose its tax lien,
      contingent upon an agreed payment schedule, which need not necessarily reflect any
      prior redemption amount. Any such agreement shall be recorded in the registry of deeds.
      This paragraph shall not be construed to obligate any municipality to make any such
      conveyance or agreement.

SECTION 5 – EXPIRATION OF AUTHORITY
The authority provided in this ordinance shall continue indefinitely, until rescinded.

judicial action, the remainder or the ordinance shall remain in full force and effect.

SECTION 7 – EFFECTIVE DATE

                  STREET LIGHT REQUEST EVALUATION CRITERIA

Purpose
The purpose of these criteria is to provide a consistent and objective framework for reviewing
resident requests for the installation of new street lighting or modifications to existing
streetlights, with a focus on public safety, traffic conditions, and fiscal responsibility.

Evaluation Criteria
1. Public Safety Need
Requests should demonstrate a clear safety concern, including but not limited to:
    • Documented vehicle crashes, near-misses, or pedestrian incidents
    • Poor nighttime visibility that contributes to unsafe conditions
    • Presence of pedestrians, cyclists, or school-age children
    • Proximity to intersections, crosswalks, curves, hills, or other roadway hazards

2. Traffic Characteristics
Consideration will be given to:
    • Traffic volume and speed
    • Road classification (local road, collector, arterial)
    • Existing traffic control devices (stop signs, signals, crosswalks)
    • Sight distance limitations

3. Pedestrian and Community Use
The Board may evaluate:
    • Sidewalk presence or absence
    • Frequency of pedestrian use
    • Proximity to schools, parks, public buildings, or transit stops
    • Residential density and neighborhood layout

4. Existing Lighting Conditions
Requests should be evaluated based on:
    • Distance to the nearest existing streetlight
    • Effectiveness of current lighting coverage
    • Whether existing lighting could be adjusted or upgraded instead of adding a new light

5. Environmental and Neighborhood Impact
Consideration should include:
    • Light pollution (per RSA 9-E:3 New Hampshire Dark Sky Policy) and spillover onto
       adjacent properties
    • Compatibility with neighborhood character


                                                                                                 Page 22 of 128
                                                                                        Agenda Item #10.2.


   •   Impact on abutters and surrounding residents

6. Cost and Fiscal Impact
The Board will consider:
    • Installation costs (ranges from $2,500-$5,000)
    • Ongoing maintenance and electricity costs (estimated at $50/per year per light)
    • Availability of funding in the current budget
    • Whether the request requires Town funding or a resident-funded option

7. Ownership and Jurisdiction
Requests must fall within:
    • Town-owned or maintained roadways
    • Areas where the Town has authority to install and maintain street lighting
      (Private roads and state-owned roadways may require separate approvals or may not be
      eligible.)

8. Alternatives to Street Lighting
The Board may recommend alternatives if appropriate, such as:
    • Reflective signage or pavement markings
    • Speed control measures
    • Vegetation trimming
    • Enforcement or traffic calming measures

Decision Outcomes
After review, the Highway Safety Advisory Board may recommend:
   • Approval of the request
   • Denial of the request
   • Approval with conditions
   • Further study or data collection
   • Implementation of alternative safety measures

Final Authority
All recommendations of the Highway Safety Advisory Board are subject to final approval by the
Town Council, in accordance with Town policy and available funding.

                               STOP SIGN GUIDELINES

1. Purpose
   The purpose of this regulation is to establish a clear, consistent, and legally defensible
   process for evaluation requests for the installation of stop signs on Town of Hooksett
   roadways. This regulation ensures compliance with state and federal standards,
   promotes traffic safety, and supports uniform enforcement.

2. Authority
   This regulation is adopted under the authority of the Town of Hooksett, recommended by
   the Highway Safety Advisory Board (HSAB) and administered by the Town Council in
   coordination with the Police Department and Department of Public Works (DPW).

   All traffic control devices within the Town shall conform to:
       • The Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD), as adopted by the
           State of New Hampshire
       • Application New Hampshire Revised Statutes Annotated (RSA)

3. Guiding Principles
      • Stop signs shall be installed only where traffic engineering criteria is met.
      • Stop signs shall not be used solely to control speed.
      • Uniform application of standards improves safety, compliance, and enforceability.
      • Unwarranted stop signs may increase rear-end crashes, reduce respect for traffic
         control devices, and divert traffic to other residential streets.

4. Applicable Standards
   The Town follows the MUTCD stop sign warrants and engineering guidance, including
   but not limited to the following criteria.

5. Stop Sign Warrants (Evaluation Criteria)
   A stop sign may be considered when one or more of the following conditions are met, as
   determined by an engineering study:
   A. Intersection Safety
       • Documented crash history indicates a pattern of right-angle or turning collisions
          that could be corrected by stop control
       • Limited sight distance that cannot be reasonably improved through vegetation
          removal, signage or roadway modification
   B. Traffic Volumes
       • Minor street experiencing significant delays entering or crossing a major street
       • Traffic volumes meeting the MUTCD guidance for multi-way stop consideration


                                                                                                Page 24 of 128
                                                                                          Agenda Item #10.2.


   C. Roadway Geometry
      • Unusual intersection configuration (offset intersections, skewed angles)
      • Steep grades or curves that limit visibility
   D. Pedestrian and School Safety
      • High pedestrian volumes crossing a roadway
      • Proximity to schools, parks, or community facilities where stop control would
         clearly enhance safety

6. Multi-Way (All-Way) Stop Control
   Multi-way stop signs may be considered when:
     • Traffic volumes on intersecting streets are approximately equal
     • Five or more correctable crashes have occurred within a 12-month period
     • An engineering study shows that multi-way stop control will improve overall
          safety and operations

7. Conditions that DO NOT Justify a Stop Sign
   The following conditions alone are not sufficient justification for installation a stop sign:
      • Speeding concerns
      • Cut-through traffic
      • Noise complaints
      • Requests based solely on neighborhood preference
      • Lack of driver courtesy

   Alternate traffic calming or enforcement measures may be recommended in these cases.

8. Request and Review Process

   Step 1: Submission
   Residents may complete a Highway Safety Request Form and submit it to the Town,
   which includes:
       • Location of the requested stop sign
       • Description of the concern
       • Any relevant observations or supporting information

   Step 2: Data Collection
   Town staff, in coordination with Police, DPW, Engineering Staff and SNHPC, may
   collect:
       • Traffic volume counts
       • Speed data
       • Crash history
       • Sight distance measurements

   Step 3: Engineering Review
   The Highway Safety Advisory Board shall work with engineering staff to review the data
   in accordance with the MUTCD standards and this regulation.

   Step 4: Recommendation
   The Board shall vote to:
      • Recommend installation to Town Council


                                                                                                   Page 25 of 128
                                                                                        Agenda Item #10.2.


          •   Recommend alternative measures to Town Council
          •   Deny the request, with reasons

       Step 5: Implementation
       If approved by Town Council, DPW shall install signage in accordance with MUTCD
       placement, size and reflectivity requirements.


Disclaimer
This regulation is intended to guide the Highway Safety Advisory Board in reviewing requests
from Town of Hooksett residents. The Town Council shall review all Board recommendations
and serves as the Town’s final authority.

Meeting:         Town Council - 13 May 2026
Department:      Administration
Staff Contact:   Leann McLaughlin, Project Coordinator

BACKGROUND INFORMATION:
PROCEDURE FOR TOWN ADMINISTRATOR ANNUAL EVALUATION
a. Council’s first meeting in May (May 13th) – Council will receive the Town Administrator’s self
evaluation to include status on his/her goals with comments for period ending June 30th of the same
fiscal year along with a blank evaluation form.

b. Council’s second meeting in May (May 27) - Councilors are to have completed and submitted their
town administrator’s evaluation form via e-mail to the designated Town Administration staff member
prior to, or are to hand deliver it at the beginning of the meeting. Councilors and the designee will
then discuss in non-public, the evaluations and will finalize them into one report by a simple majority
vote. Only town councilors and the designee will be in attendance during this non-public session to
discuss and finalize the evaluation of the Town Administrator. The Town Administrator will receive the
evaluation from the council at this meeting

c. Council’s first meeting in June (June 10) - Council will discuss the evaluation report with the Town
Administrator

d. Annually at the first meeting in July (July 8) - the Administrator’s goals will be an agenda item. The
Council and the Administrator shall define such goals and performance objectives which they
determine necessary for the proper operation of the Town and the attainment of the Council’s policy
objectives and shall further establish a relative priority among those various goals and objectives,
said goals and objectives to be reduced in writing. They shall generally be attainable within the time
limitations as specified and the annual operating capital budgets and evaluation. If goals are not
concluded, the Council will hold a special meeting a week later to finalize the goals.


POLICY IMPLICATIONS:
TA Evaluation procedure is as outlined in the Town council Rules of Procedure as amended May 24,
2024.

RECOMMENDATION:
Review the procedure for Town Administrator's review and prepare.

ATTACHMENTS:

STAFF REPORT

To:              Town Council
Title:           Police Radio Console upgrade
Meeting:         Town Council - 13 May 2026
Department:      Town Council
Staff Contact:   Justin Sargent, Chief of Police

BACKGROUND INFORMATION:
The town voted to utilize money from the Fund balance in the amount of up to $250,000.00 to
purchase a new dispatch radio console (Article 13). This console will be purchased from Ossipee
Mountain Electronics our radio vendor who is working off State Bid pricing for this console. I am
looking for the council to allow the Police Department to utilize these funds on July 1st, 2026 to
purchase this new radio console. The reason for this coming in front of Council now is to have
Ossipee Mountain Electronics start to order the system for install in early July.

FINANCIAL IMPACT:
Up to $250,000.00 from the Town's Fund Balance as stated in Article 13 of this years vote.

POLICY IMPLICATIONS:
None

RECOMMENDATION:
I recommend this purchase as it was approved by the town voters.

SUGGESTED MOTION:
Accept the motion to spend up to $250,000.00 on the Hooksett Police Departments Radio Console
Replacement.

I agree with the suggested motion.

STAFF REPORT

To:            Town Council
Title:         Update on FY 2026-27 Property & Liability and Workers' Compensation Insurance
               coverages.
Meeting:       Town Council - 13 May 2026
Department:    Finance
Staff Contact: Christine Tewksbury, Finance Director

BACKGROUND INFORMATION:
In the fall of 2025, the Town received renewal rates for the upcoming budget year 2026-27 for both
Property & Liability and Workers' Compensation insurance from Primex, our current provider.
Property & Liability                                            Workers' Compensation
FY 2025-26        $318,230                                     FY 2025-26    $345,158
FY 2026-27        $419,427                                     FY 2026-27    $368,491
Increase          $101,197 or 32%                              Increase     $ 23,313 or .07%

In 2021 the Town bid out these coverages and only received one bid, which was Primex.

To increase the chance of getting more bids, the Town worked with Jeff Reardon of Noyes Insurance.
He reached out to potential carriers but was unable to secure any quotes, stating both coverages
show a high loss ratio. Property & liability loss ratio is 130% and workers’ compensation had a high
loss ratio in 2021.


RECOMMENDATION:
No motion needed.

TOWN ADMINISTRATOR'S RECOMMENDATION:
Listen to Finance Director's presentation on this matter.

Primex FY 2026-27 renewal worksheets

Town Council
STAFF REPORT

To:               Town Council
Title:            Budget Preparation Advisory Committee
Meeting:          Town Council - 13 May 2026
Department:       Administration
Staff Contact:    André Garron, Town Administrator

BACKGROUND INFORMATION:
Town Council received a question through its Public Input segment of the April 22, 2026 Town
Council agenda. The question asked was, Can Town Council create a Budget Preparation
Committee" that would provide input on the budget development process of the budget review. The
answer from Town Council was yes, through Article 11, subsection D. "Other Administrative
Committees. Other administrative boards and committees may be established as necessary by the
Town Council.

Atty, Serge, via email dated April 28, 2026, "
Hi, Andre. Would this advisory committee be focused on the Town budget? If you can provide some more
detail about what this advisory committee would be expected to do that will help my analysis.

Obviously, the elected Budget Committee has specific roles and responsibilities under RSA 32:16 so an
advisory committee should not be duplicating those roles. But if this new committee is essentially focusing on
ways to develop the Town budget that the TC will then review and incorporate as it prepares the final Town
budget that goes to the Budget Committee, I think that is fine. Article 11.1, Section D does give the TC wide
latitude in appointing other administrative committees so I think this advisory committee would be included in
that.

Let me know if you have additional questions. Thanks.

-Matt "

FINANCIAL IMPACT:
N/A

POLICY IMPLICATIONS:
As long as the new budget advisory committee does not infringe upon the statutory requirements of
the Budget Committee, then the create of this new advisory committee is possible.

TOWN ADMINISTRATOR'S RECOMMENDATION:
Discussion on the creation of this new committee, membership, and timeline for delivery of outcome
of the committee.

65          Public Hearing for Adoption of New Ordinance #26-02 Sale of Tax Deeded Property "as justice
66          may require"
67
68   André Garron, Town Administrator: RSA 80:80, III governs how a municipality handles tax liens and tax
69   deeded property. RSA 80:80 contains a provision that allows the governing body to authorize the
70   disposal of tax liens or tax deeded property in alternative ways beyond public auction or sealed bid --
71   "as justice may require." The phrase "as justice may require" is a provision that gives the Town Council
72   discretion to dispose of tax liens or tax deeded property in ways other than public auction or sealed
73   bid, when circumstances justify it. Specifically, the section of RSA 80:80, III, states, "III. The governing
74   body may, by a specific article in the town warrant, or by ordinance, be authorized to dispose of liens
75   or tax deeded properties in a manner other than as provided in this section, as justice may require.
76   Before proceeding under this provision, the governing body shall make an affirmative finding that
77   disposal by a method other than sealed bid or public auction is in the public interest.
78
79   T. Tsantoulis: Noted that this seems like it could increase tax revenue for town by having land claimed
80   to be back on the tax roll and taxes being paid on it
81
82   R. Duhaime: Noted concern 4(b) regarding affordable housing developments and the Town Council
83   making decision without Planning and Zoning Boards involved.
84
85   A. Garron: Noted that if Town Council votes to allow a sale to move forward, it doesn’t prevent it from
86   going through the process for development. The Town Council would not be approving affordable
87   housing.
88
89   J. Sullivan: Agreed with the concern and asked for additional language that could be added to address
90   this concern?
